home.title: Really learn C#. Then make your own game.
home.lead: A short bit of theory, then a task right away. Code runs right in the browser, and tests honestly tell you what works.

runner.loading: Loading the C# compiler. The first time takes a few seconds.
runner.timeout: The program ran too long, so we stopped it. Maybe it has an endless loop — a loop whose condition never becomes false.
runner.crashed: The compiler stopped unexpectedly. Try running again.
runner.outputLimit: The program printed too much text, so we stopped it. Maybe printing is inside an endless loop.

compiler.unknown: The compiler found an error. Its explanation is below.
compiler.CS1002: A semicolon «;» is missing. In C# every command ends with «;» — that is how the computer knows where it ends.
compiler.CS0103: The name «{arg0}» was not found. Check that it is declared above and has no typo. C# tells capital and small letters apart: «hp» and «HP» are different names.
compiler.CS0246: The type «{arg0}» was not found. A type is a kind of data: int is a whole number, string is text. Check the spelling.
compiler.CS0029: A value of type {arg0} can't go into a variable of type {arg1}. For example, text in quotes is a string, not a number.
compiler.CS0266: A value of type {arg0} can't just go into {arg1}: some data may be lost — for example, the fractional part of a number.
compiler.CS0165: The variable «{arg0}» is used, but nothing has been put into it yet. Assign a value before reading a variable.
compiler.CS0128: The variable «{arg0}» is already declared above. To declare means to write a type and a name; you don't need to do it twice.
compiler.CS1010: The text is not closed: a quote «"» is missing at the end of the line.
compiler.CS1513: A closing curly brace «{'}'}» is missing. Every «{'{'}» needs its pair.
compiler.CS1026: A closing parenthesis «)» is missing. Every «(» needs its pair.
compiler.CS0117: {arg0} has no «{arg1}». Check the spelling: C# tells capital and small letters apart.
compiler.CS1061: A value of type {arg0} has no «{arg1}». Check the spelling: C# tells capital and small letters apart.
compiler.CS0019: The operation «{arg0}» can't be done with values of types {arg1} and {arg2}. For example, you can't subtract a number from text.
compiler.CS1501: The method «{arg0}» doesn't take this many arguments ({arg1}). Arguments are the values in parentheses when you call a method.
compiler.CS0161: The method {arg0} must return a value, but there is a case where it ends without return.
compiler.CS0201: This line does nothing. A command can be, for example, an assignment (hp = 10) or a method call (Console.WriteLine(hp)).
compiler.CS1525: «{arg0}» can't be here: a value or an expression is needed in this place.
compiler.CS0219: A value was put into the variable «{arg0}», but it is never used after that.
compiler.CS0168: The variable «{arg0}» is declared but never used.
compiler.CS8773: This is only allowed in C# {arg1} and newer. We learn C# 9 — the version Unity understands.
compiler.CS8803: Program commands must come before class declarations: commands first, classes at the end of the file.
compiler.CS5001: The program has no commands to run. Add at least one, for example printing with Console.WriteLine.

runtime.unknown: The program stopped with the error {type}.
runtime.DivideByZeroException: Division by zero. A whole number can't be divided by zero — check the divisor.
runtime.IndexOutOfRangeException: The array has no element with this number. Numbers (indexes) start at 0: in an array of 3 elements the last one is 2.
runtime.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: A number is out of the allowed range. For example, a list element number is bigger than the number of elements.
runtime.NullReferenceException: Access to an empty value (null): the variable doesn't point to anything.
runtime.FormatException: The text couldn't be turned into a number. For example, int.Parse("ten") won't work — it needs "10".
runtime.OverflowException: The number is too big or too small for this type.
runtime.InvalidCastException: The value can't be turned into this type.
runtime.KeyNotFoundException: The dictionary has no such key.
runtime.InvalidOperationException: This action can't be done right now. For example, taking the first element of an empty list.
